exposure: mode of delivery (unassisted vaginal, labouring lower segment caesarean section, prelabour lower segment caesarean section)
outcome: differentially expressed inflammatory genes (IL1RL1, STAT1, STAT2, IL2RB, IL17RE, IL18BP, TNFAIP2, TNFSF10, TNFRSF8)
common inflammasome genes (IL1B, IL1R1, IL1R2, IL6, IL18, IL18R1, IL10, IL33)
cohort: Placental chorionic villus samples were collected from women delivering at term via unassisted vaginal birth, labouring lower segment caesarean section, or prelabour lower segment caesarean section.
finding: Placental inflammasome activation differs significantly based on the mode of delivery and neonatal sex.
mod_finding: Placentae from UV births expressed pro-inflammatory mediators, LLSCS births demonstrated a much greater pro-inflammatory response with interplay of pro- and anti-inflammatory mediators, and inflammasome activation was very low in placentae from PLSCS births.
